correctness.rationale: The probability latitude integral is sinc(at) on a sphere of radius a, so the normalized mixture is one at zero and at nonzero zeros has the same multiplicity as H=sin(t)+sin(rt)/r. H_t factors into two cosines. If either vanishes, sin(t)=±sin(rt); because r is strictly between zero and one the coefficient 1±1/r cannot vanish, and both sines must vanish at a repeated zero. The integer phases are opposite in parity exactly at odd multiples of qπ for a reduced opposite-parity pair p,q. There H_tt vanishes and H_ttt=cos(⁠t₀)(r₀²−1) is nonzero, so the root contributes exactly two to multiplicity minus distinct count. Also H_r=−cos(t₀)t₀/r₀ there. Substituting δ=u³ and t−t₀=uw into the analytic expansion leaves a holomorphic quotient by u³ whose limiting cubic has three distinct roots with C³=6t₀/[r₀(r₀²−1)]. The simple-root implicit function theorem and a fixed-disk Rouché count give three simple roots with the stated error; conjugation fixes the real branch and exchanges the two off-axis branches. This is an analytic all-parameter check, not reliance on the recorded numerical examples.
residual_risks: Fixed t₀,r₀ for the detuning theorem; no uniform estimate as frequency increases or r₀ approaches one. No individual zero-count asymptotic inferred.

value.rationale: For a natural positive radial model built from just two probability shells, the result specifies exactly when radial signals have higher-order nulls, their locations and multiplicity excess, and which nearby complex zeros remain real when the radius is detuned. The sharp parity boundary excludes all other ratios and repeated real roots, and the coefficient quantifies sensitivity to radius. This is more than the classical spherical transform or citing generic Puiseux scaling.
residual_risks: Value is for the equal-mass two-shell setting and its exact instability, not a general theory for more shells or dimensions.
